name: flying-splice
title: Flying Splice
description: A logo ribbon whose real subject is the flying paster on a web press: two roll stands, side by side, unwind a ribbon of marks at constant web speed — the running roll's radius falls from 64.6px to 27.5px as its RPM more than doubles (1.06 -> 2.48 rev/s), and every 22s the spun-up standby roll splices in mid-flight while a knife severs the spent roll and a fresh one rises into its place.
useWhen: a logo ribbon where the moving subject is a supply-side mechanism running down over time, not the strip of marks itself. Reach for ticker-tape-splice instead when the splice is an event ON the strip with no supply side at all (new data arriving, a 1px seam riding with it) — flying-splice has no equivalent 'new item arrives' API, its splice happens because a roll ran out. Reach for logo-cloud-settle instead for a static/settling grid of marks with no continuous feed motion at all.
instruction: Build <FlyingSplice paused? className? style?> as a 2D canvas band (never full-bleed) whose dominant visual is two paper-roll stands, not the ribbon. GEOMETRY: M = min(bandW, bandH), W = bandW; R_max = max(0.19*M, 0.075*W) (the 0.075*W floor only engages on very wide bands and exists so the two-roll cluster clears the hard 30%-of-band-width kill criterion at any aspect ratio; at typical/card aspect ratios the 0.19*M branch wins, giving the spec's checkable 64.6px at M=340); R_splice = R_max * (27.5/64.6). The two stands sit side by side near the right edge of the band with a small gap between them; the ribbon and its nip point (paster arm + knife) sit to their left, so marks are 'printed' at the nip and scroll right-to-left, away from the rolls that produced them. RADIUS/RPM, the actual mechanic: under constant web speed v = 0.42*W px/s, the running roll's radius is the exact closed form r(t) = sqrt(R_max^2 - B*t) with B = (R_max^2 - R_splice^2)/22.0 (a 22.0s cycle, unbounded, never terminating), and its swept angle is the exact integral theta(t) = 2*v*(R_max - r(t))/B — both closed-form, never a per-frame accumulator, because prefers-reduced-motion must render exactly STATIC_TIME=22.09s byte-stably without simulating from t=0. RPM climbs 1.06 -> 2.48 rev/s (more than doubles) as radius falls 64.6 -> 27.5px; each roll carries 4 radial index lines (3 below M=200px, alongside 6 marks instead of 9) rotating at theta(t) so the spin-up is legible rather than blurring, and the roll's own shrinking outer boundary IS the visible 'wrap edge' receding toward the core — no separate element needed. CYCLE MODEL: cycle = floor(t/22), phase = t - 22*cycle, runningStandIndex = cycle % 2 — the two stands swap running/standby roles every cycle by construction, so the stand that was standby simply continues unwinding as the new running roll with no special-casing (its radius/angle formulas already evaluate correctly starting from R_max/0 at phase 0). The OTHER stand (standby role) spends phase < ~3.13s of cycles after the first playing the spent-roll choreography: decelerating from omega = v/R_splice to 0 over 1.1s via the closed-form quadratic ease-in integral, dropping out of frame (translateY + fade over 400ms), a 900ms gap, then a fresh R_max roll rising back into place over 700ms (quadratic ease-out). For the rest of the cycle it sits idle at R_max until phase >= 18.6s, when it spins up to matched surface speed (omega = v/R_max) over the final 3.4s via the closed-form quadratic ease-out integral — continuity between spin-up and the following running phase is exact because the running phase's angle offset is the spin-up's own total swept angle, not a reset to zero. SPLICE MOMENT: a shared paster-arm silhouette (a --foreground line pivoting near the nip) swings 26deg over its final 180ms of the cycle, completing contact exactly at the cycle wrap, and holds briefly into the new cycle before retracting; a knife bar sweeps across the nip in a 120ms window centred on 90ms into the new cycle (reconciling the spec's 'fires 90ms after contact' with its 'static frame is mid-sweep' — a window merely started at 90ms would only just be beginning). At that same instant a chevron splice tape (two diagonal bands at +/-34deg from cross-web, each 0.03*W wide) is stamped onto the ribbon at the nip and scrolls left at v(t) for 2.4s like any mark. WEB: the ribbon is a visible strip of paper, not free-floating marks — a paper-coloured band of height 1.95*markSize centred on the band, running from the left edge to just inside the running roll's CURRENT radius (anchored to the stand centre it juts out past a run-down roll as a bare rectangle), with darker hairline edges; the marks ride on it and the splice tape is clipped to it. Each stand also carries a post and foot below its roll, and the running stand carries a dashed capacity ring at R_max, so the gap between that ring and the roll's wrap edge makes the run-down legible in a single still instead of only across 22s of motion. RIBBON: marks are drawn from a fixed seeded PRNG (mulberry32, not Math.random) so the pattern is identical on every mount — required for reduced-motion byte-stability. Each mark is one of three abstract placeholder families (concentric arcs, a bar cluster, a lattice), 0.14*M wide, spaced 0.155*W apart, generated purely from x = nipX - ((v(t)*t) mod spacing) stepping backward — never accumulated per-frame state — so a mark only ever exists downstream of the nip. TOKENS: getComputedStyle(documentElement) for --background/--foreground/--border read as the FIRST statement inside the mount effect, before the ResizeObserver is constructed or anything paints, re-read on a MutationObserver watching documentElement's class; a `colorsReady` guard makes draw() a no-op until that first read completes on all three entry paths (rAF start, ResizeObserver's initial fire, IntersectionObserver resume). Ribbon/roll paper is mix(background, foreground, 0.13 light / 0.34 dark) — at 0.16 the rolls are near-black discs on a near-black band and the mechanism is invisible however correct its motion; marks are foreground at 0.78 alpha; roll bodies are shaded by a shallow offset radial gradient standing in for a single-lamp Lambert term (azimuth 118deg, offset 0.22r, +0.10/-0.12 lightness — a deeper offset reads as a billiard ball rather than the flat end of a wound coil) over a --background hub disc at 0.17r plus sparse concentric ring banding for a wound-paper read — value only, no hue. The chevron tape is a -0.14 lightness band with a +0.09 lightness leading hairline and is the single highest-risk spot for the accent defect, so --ns-accent never appears on it, on the ribbon, or on the rolls; --border appears only as the band's top/bottom hairlines. CANVAS: DPR capped at 2, ResizeObserver on the host element (not window), rAF paused on IntersectionObserver offscreen and visibilitychange, prefers-reduced-motion (or the paused prop) freezes on the single composed frame at STATIC_TIME=22.09s (arm down, knife mid-sweep, chevron just entering, both rolls turning at visibly different radii/index-line spacing) rather than t=0, which would show only one spinning disc beside a static one. No pointer interaction of any kind — hover/pointer highlights on a rotating disc are exactly the accent-on-the-climactic-moment defect this component's spec calls out by name.
